## Class

In job `100874330553`:

```
assert b'{\r\n  "bin…": 2\r\n}\r\n' == b'{\n  "bindi…sion": 2\n}\n'
```

Python's text mode translates `\n` to `\r\n` on write under Windows unless `newline=""` is passed.
rebar writes JSON artifacts (a binding store snapshot here) and then compares them **byte-exactly**
against an expected form — signatures, digests, and snapshot equality all depend on those bytes.

This is not cosmetic. A `\r\n`-translated artifact has a **different sha256** from the same logical
content on POSIX, so an attestation or snapshot digest computed on Windows will not match one
computed on Linux. That is a correctness defect in the signing/snapshot path, surfaced by a test.

Git's `core.autocrlf` may compound it independently of Python's text mode; check both.

## What the fix must decide

Artifacts whose bytes are load-bearing (anything hashed, signed, or compared) must be written with
explicit `newline=""` (or in binary mode) so their bytes are platform-independent. Human-facing
console output may keep native line endings. Draw that line explicitly and enforce it.

## Blocked by S1

## Proving command

```
uv run --no-sync pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q -p no:cacheprovider 2>&1 \
  | grep -c '\\\\r\\\\n'   # must be 0
```
on `windows-latest`, plus the decisive cross-platform proof: a test that writes the binding-store
snapshot and asserts its sha256 equals a hard-coded digest — identical on Windows and Linux.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Zero CRLF byte-comparison failures in a Windows sweep.
2. A hashed artifact produces the same digest on Windows and Linux, asserted by a test.
